# security-openbao-seal-static

<!-- BEGIN DECLARED (generated by scripts/wiki-compile.py — do not edit) -->

> Source comment, verbatim from `kustomization.yaml`:
>
> OpenBao static-key auto-unseal — applied on top of security/openbao via components:
>
> Adds:
> - seal "static" config (ConfigMap openbao-seal-config), passed as a second -config
> - Secret volume openbao-seal-key mounted read-only at /openbao/seal
>
> The pod unseals itself on every start. The trade-off: the key lives in the
> cluster. Whoever can read Secret openbao-seal-key plus the raft PVC can read
> the data. Use Shamir (the default) if a human at every restart is acceptable.
>
> This component never ships the key. The tenant supplies Secret openbao-seal-key
> (SealedSecret, External Secrets from another store, or out of band) with:
> current.key   32 random bytes (required)
> previous.key  the prior key (only while rotating)
> openssl rand -out current.key 32
> kubectl -n security create secret generic openbao-seal-key --from-file=current.key
>
> Usage in overlay kustomization.yaml:
> resources:
> - path/to/security/openbao
> components:
> - path/to/security/openbao/seal-static
>
> Key rotation (n-1 -> n). "The key id MUST always match the underlying key."
> 1. Add the new key to the Secret as current.key and move the old one to previous.key
> 2. Patch ConfigMap openbao-seal-config to:
> seal "static" {
> current_key_id  = "key-2"
> current_key     = "file:///openbao/seal/current.key"
> previous_key_id = "key-1"
> previous_key    = "file:///openbao/seal/previous.key"
> }
> 3. Restart the pod (kubectl -n security delete pod openbao-0). Config is read at start.
> 4. Once it has unsealed with the new key, drop previous_* and previous.key and restart again.
>
> Applies to NEW instances. Converting an instance already initialized with Shamir
> is a seal migration (`disabled = "true"` on the old seal, `bao operator unseal -migrate`),
> not a patch.
>
> Assumes the openbao container is containers[0] of the StatefulSet.
>
> No `namespace:` here on purpose. A Component's namespace applies to everything the
> consuming kustomization holds, not only to its own resources: it would move a
> tenant's other resources into `security`. The resources below carry
> `namespace: security` themselves, like the base, and a tenant overlay's
> `namespace:` moves them along with it.
